title: SETA shared sparse subspace + Mirror views
hypothesis: After shared coordinates are discovered from prior tasks, a compact task-coordinate basis inside that shared sparse region reduces payload growth without increasing held-out task error compared with SETA-style shared/private storage; generic PCA may explain it.
physical_object: one shared sparse coordinate region plus task-specific sparse residuals
mirror_coordinate: low-rank task code over shared-coordinate weight matrix
logical_multiplicity: eight linear task functions with a common sparse support and private coordinates

model.evaluation: oracle task deltas encoded then reconstructed; 128 held-out random query inputs assess functional reconstruction

controls: SETA-style shared support plus private sparse residual
Mirror shared basis and task code

development.selection_metric: shared-support recovery, query NRMSE, actual serialized bytes

fresh.selection_metric: frozen reconstruction error and serialized bytes

storage.authority: actual serialized bytes; sparse index and value payloads, basis and codes all charged

success_gate: At least 20% byte reduction vs SETA-style shared/private storage at query NRMSE <=0.05; Mirror-specific value additionally requires beating generic PCA.
failure_gate: No byte reduction at matched quality, or Mirror is matched by generic PCA; support discovery errors make result NOT ESTABLISHED.
boundaries: Synthetic sparse linear task functions only
SETA mechanism is approximated, not a faithful continual-learning reproduction
No catastrophic forgetting or routing evidence
Task vectors are given to encoder; this is compression/reconstruction, not task learning
